extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent applicants, and patent counsel advising on international prosecution
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for obtaining accelerated examination through Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) programs between patent offices, covering eligibility, filing requirements, office-specific procedures, timing, risks, and prosecution strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected benefits of PPH
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH programs seem to at least increase allowance rates and reduce a number of office actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: USPTO reported a PPH application allowance rate of about 94% (more than double usual), and average number of office actions approximately half of other U.S. patent applications; CIPO reported ~35% of PPH applications deemed allowable without an examiner’s report, many others requiring only correction of informalities. Benefits include accelerated patent grant, high allowance rates, and potential cost savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic eligibility requirements for PPH entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Not every application is eligible; a number of requirements must be met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial conditions: (1) the application must be an application claiming priority under the Paris Convention, a National Stage of a PCT application, or a bypass continuation application; (2) the application must have at least one claim allowed by the Office of First Filing (OFF); (3) claims provided to the Office of Second Filing (OSF) must correspond in scope to the claims found to be allowable in the OFF; (4) examination of the application must not have yet begun in the OSF. If these are met, an applicant can file a Request for participation in the PPH program.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO-specific PPH filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When USPTO is the OSF, additional documentary and procedural submissions are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required: Request for participation, petition to make special and required petition fee, copies of all office actions from the OFF relevant to patentability (with translations if in a foreign language), a table indicating correspondence between each claim in the OSF application and an allowed claim from the OFF, and an information disclosure statement listing all documents cited by the OFF. If OFF is EPO or JPO, applicant can request USPTO obtain documents electronically via Dossier Access System. USPTO will review submissions and give one chance to bring the application into compliance if found lacking. If granted, the application is examined in advance; any amendments must still correspond to one or more allowable claims from the OFF as shown in a new correspondence table filed with the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPO-specific PPH rules and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: EPO-USPTO PPH was a trial program with specific limitations and submission requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points: EPO PPH not open to ex-PCT applications that have entered the European phase (excluding many U.S.-priority applications). For eligible EPO applications, applicant will be invited to amend claims to conform to corresponding U.S. patent claims; original or amended claims must sufficiently correspond in scope to patentable/allowable claims in the USPTO application and a claims correspondence chart must be filed. Applicant must submit copies of all USPTO office actions relevant to patentability and copies of all documents cited in the USPTO office action except European patents/published European applications (unless already filed in the U.S. application, in which case a reference is sufficient). When granted by EPO, application is advanced and processed under PACE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office-specific variability in PPH procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each OSF follows its own rules and practices; eligibility requirements and application procedures vary among PPH programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different OSFs may carry out different fast-track procedures (e.g., JPO accelerates only the first round of examination to issue a first action within 2-3 months). Eligibility and procedural differences may even exist between OFF and OSF within the same PPH program. It is therefore important to check current PPH requirements and procedures in each OSF of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing/window for filing PPH requests
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a narrow window of opportunity for entry into a PPH program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application must not have been filed so recently that prosecution in the OFF has not reached a successful conclusion, nor filed so long ago that examination has already begun in the OSF. Applicants must monitor prosecution status of related OFF and OSF applications and file a PPH request as soon as an allowance issues in the OFF, before an examination report or office action issues in the desired OSF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk that OFF-allowed claims won't be allowable in OSF
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims allowed by the OFF under their patent laws and rules might not be allowable under the patent laws/rules of the OSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: an amendment to overcome a U.S. rejection under 35 U.S.C. §102(e) may not be required in the EPO; differing standards for obviousness (U.S.) and inventive step (other jurisdictions) may lead to no allowable corresponding claim in OSF. Also, amendments made during OFF prosecution could narrow claims more than necessary for OSF, and negative comments by an OSF examiner might be used against the OFF-granted patent in litigation. Applicants trade off claim breadth/admissions for earlier examination and potential earlier enforceable protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic considerations for maximizing PPH benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should develop prosecution strategies to maximize advantages and mitigate disadvantages of PPH programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider subject matter, priority relationships, claim scope, and timing. Specific strategic actions: identify eligible pairs of OFF and OSF applications; identify potential future OFF/OSF pairs; choose preferred OFF or OSF; manage prosecution timelines to increase eligibility chances; identify subject matter, claims, and claim formats suitable for each PPH program; preserve ability to protect other inventions outside PPH programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of continuation/divisional practice to manage trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuation or divisional filings can be used so PPH examination applies to some claims while preserving broader claims elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: In an unexamined U.S. application with claims to multiple inventions, claims corresponding to allowable OFF claims can be examined under PPH while claims to other inventions are filed in divisional/continuation applications to be prosecuted separately. An applicant can file a continuation from the U.S. application and request that the continuation be examined under PPH, preserving broader claims in the first U.S. application for conventional prosecution while accelerating others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when USPTO is the OFF
rubrics_metrics.description: If USPTO is the OFF, other OSFs can accept PPH Requests based on claims found allowable in the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A PPH Request can be filed in the OSF for fast-track examination of claims that correspond to claims found allowable in the USPTO. Each OSF will then follow its own rules and practices during examination of the claims presented in the OSF application.
